title: Daylight-aligned hydration
summary: Front-load fluids earlier in the day and taper large volumes before sleep so timing supports energy and sleep architecture.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Daylight-aligned hydration means shifting when you drink—not only how much. Front-load glasses earlier in the waking day; taper large volumes in the last hours before bed. You practice the intentional timing habit, not every sip.

sections.heading: Why timing matters
sections.body: Late large volumes can fragment sleep with bathroom trips. Morning and daytime hydration support the circadian day when you are upright, moving, and in light. When you drink can matter as much as what you drink for sleep quality and daytime energy. This is behavioral sleep hygiene meeting the Water pillar.

sections.heading: Practical habit
sections.body: Move your biggest glasses toward morning and midday. Keep evening sips smaller unless thirst or medical needs say otherwise. Pair the first daylight glass with Low-D morning hydration outdoors or by an open door when that is your keystone. Do not confuse “taper before bed” with chronic under-drinking in heat or training.

sections.heading: What is solid vs framework
sections.body: Solid ground: nocturia from late fluids can worsen sleep; daytime hydration supports normal function. Framework: that exact minute schedules of water “charge” mitochondria independent of light, food, and sleep. Timing is a practical lever—not a mystical dose.

sections.heading: How to use it here
sections.body: Practice Daylight-aligned hydration when you deliberately shifted timing—earlier glasses, less late chugging. Pair with Drinking water practice and Low-D morning hydration for a full Water day. Educational only—not medical advice for fluid restriction in heart or kidney disease.
